title: Ai sli gaming?
author: Inevitable-4522
selftext:
Ive been seeing a lot more ai coding done with games being mashed together,  this got me wondering if any work has been done on getting games to run on sli again? With the insane prices of gpus, would be really nice to be able to harness the processing of multiple cards. I know there is a steam app that let's you use a second gpu for frame gen, but true sli would be amazing, even if the gains arent 2x. 

Just looking around at prices and figures, a used 4090 is like $4500 cad, with a performance boost of 79% (aprox) over a 3080ti, a card that is like $500-$700.

comments.author: GraphXGames
comments.body: This is not profitable for graphics card manufacturers, so you won't gain any advantage.

replies.author: Inevitable-4522
replies.body:
I forgot this why I dont post on reddit anymore... I need to write a novel for people grasp a concept that anyone else would understand, and even if i do there will be people still managing to get confused. 

Im not asking if ubisoft is working on sli in any of their new games. Or if Nvidia is making a program...  Im asking if the community of people currently using ai on things like mashing two existing games together have seen anyone working on getting sli to work on games.

replies.author: GraphXGames
replies.body: Graphics card manufacturers themselves have abandoned the Multi-GPU concept; SLI is no longer supported on new graphics cards.

replies.author: Inevitable-4522
replies.body:
You can still use multi gpus today. Its very common in VFX work for renders. I currently have 2 3080tis in my pc, I can use both of them on a single ai application,  or run two different ones at once, depending on how the program was designed. 

That's why im inquiring about people using ai to work on game code to bring multi gpu functionality back. Game devs weren't intending on having mw2 mashed into Minecraft, but ai devs figures that out, maybe there is work being done to get multi gpu support again?

replies.author: GraphXGames
replies.body: If the UE5/Unity engines don’t support this, then no one is going to do it manually. And game engines won’t do this because the DirectX/Vulkan APIs themselves don’t do it. And DirectX/Vulkan don’t do this because there is no universal hardware support.

replies.author: Inevitable-4522
replies.body: I already dont care about your opinion dude, you struggled to grasp this entire interaction so what you said has zero credibility.

replies.author: GraphXGames
replies.body:
NVIDIA SLI technology is completely dead for the consumer and gaming market. Its official demise occurred back in 2021, when NVIDIA finally stopped adding new SLI profiles at the driver level.

A single modern flagship graphics card is more powerful, more energy-efficient, and more stable than any bulky, multi-card setup from the previous generation.

replies.author: EdOfO
replies.body:
They've very calmly and thoroughly explained to you why this isn't done despite your insults.  
  
People mash 4 cards together to run local AI models now and even they don't bother using that to supercharge their games or the latest DLSS.   
  
There are good reasons why the entire industry dropped SLI long ago and your question came down to "We can buy two cards, so why not?"  
Spending a little bit of time first reading why SLI was abandoned would have explained it.

replies.author: Inevitable-4522
replies.body:
Plenty of people use DLSS and frame gen with a second card... but that's not the question.  And they arent going to be able to supercharge their games if the code doesnt even support it. Saying "its not profitable for gpu manufacturers" isnt answering my question, im asking about ai not what the manufacturers are currently doing.

This is just them doing that very strange, very reddit thing of having to rewrite the question in their head so they can hear themselves talk, while taking over both roles of the conversation.  

I also had looked into why sli wasnt a thing anymore, and the answers didnt seem to rule out potential benifits from ai doing work that devs didnt implement.

replies.author: EdOfO
replies.body:
Thank you for the more respectful response. I appreciate it.  
## Let's think of all the issues:  
1. If "SLI" comes back, it won't be using the SLI method as that technology *hit a bottleneck a long time ago.* A new multi-card tech will need new drivers and new development made by NVIDIA who doesn't seem interested yet. 
2. It will also require game developers to program specifically for it and Unreal & Unity & Microsoft & Khronos to spend a lot of time developing and adding support for it before that. 
3. The entire industry has moved to low power low heat high efficiency cards since. PCs use ARM now!  
Adding 2x or 4x GPU cards for the top 0.1% of gamers who will spend ten thousand on their liquid cooled machine doesn't make any sense to me. Does it still make a lot of sense to you? It may happen when those setups hit over 1% adoption but memory prices have to come way down first. 16+ months from now I expect. *Then* 1-2 happens. 
4. Game graphics haven't improved much in the last few years to require what it does. Is an 8k monitor at 240Hz and 240 fps for a million poly game that important to anybody really? I haven't heard anybody talk about great new graphics being the wow required feature in years.   Framerate is what SLI is for **and again that tech hit a bottleneck a long time ago.**  
Good VR requires this, but its adoption is ass. 
5. If a multi-card support is developed, it will likely be to separate different graphics and processing features onto separate cards. For example, upscaling or DLSS or AI behavior onto one and everything else onto another. Things like this: https://youtu.be/yoEsuZyltFc?si=KM02wE_gi2qB2f1Z  
Why it hasn't, see reasons 1-3.
